data.title: CFTC Guidance Requires at Least 20% Haircuts for Bitcoin and Ether in Operating Reserves
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission staff issued guidance on using crypto assets in operating reserves, requiring Bitcoin and ether to be valued with at least a 20% haircut and eligible payment stablecoins with a 2% haircut. The guidance also says these assets cannot count toward the minimum liquidity requirement for operating resources.

data.title: AI | Katy Kaminski Says NVDA Surge Shows AI Trade’s Reach After Huang Returns
data.description: Katy Kaminski, chief research strategist and portfolio manager at AlphaSimplex Group, said Nvidia’s sharp jump underscored how concentrated and pervasive the AI trade has become, with influence extending beyond equities, according to Bloomberg. She said the scale of recent market moves showed the theme’s importance. Kaminski spoke with Romaine Bostick on “The Close.”

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Emily Kilcrease Criticizes Nvidia’s Decision to Reinstate Jensen Huang
data.description: Emily Kilcrease criticized Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, saying allegations of possible chip diversion and Chinese influence are serious and warrant a thorough investigation, according to Bloomberg. She said only about two weeks had passed since the revelations became public, leaving too little time to establish whether national security concerns exist. Kilcrease spoke with Romaine Bostick on “The Close.”

data.title: UTXO Management’s Loren Asmus Says Bitcoin Is an Excellent Entry Point, Long-Term Thesis Unchanged
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Bitcoin Magazine, UTXO Management executive Loren Asmus said Bitcoin’s long-term investment thesis remains intact despite a weak year for its price performance, describing current conditions as an “excellent entry point.” He said the thesis and protocol have not changed and that Bitcoin is not going away.

Asmus said UTXO Management is developing investment vehicles to make Bitcoin more accessible to institutions and asset allocators over the next 10 to 20 years. He also discussed Bitcoin’s potential role as a hedge, the simultaneous declines in stocks, gold and Bitcoin, and topics including a rebound from a two-year low, AI-related trading and capital flows, miner selling, digital asset treasury companies, ETF outflows, tax-loss harvesting, portfolio rebalancing, sovereign wealth funds’ bear-market strategies, and ETF adoption and 1% allocations.

data.title: AMD Registers 337 Million Shares for Future Sale by Shareholders
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, AMD filed documents with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to register up to 337 million shares for future sale by shareholders, including 160 million shares each for OpenAI and Meta Platforms. The shares will be unlocked gradually based on AMD chip purchase progress and share-price targets, and are not yet eligible for exercise.

data.title: Fed's John Williams: Higher Rates Likely Over Time to Address Inflation
data.description: According to CNBC, Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said Monday that policymakers need to take further action over time to bring inflation under control. He expects inflation to move closer to the Fed's 2% target in 2027 and reach it the following year, and said there is little evidence that artificial intelligence will cause more persistent inflation. The Federal Open Market Committee meets Dec. 8-9, and markets were fully pricing in a quarter percentage point increase from the current target range of 3.75%-4%. Williams did not explicitly address the December meeting.

data.title: AI | Patrick McHenry: Jensen Huang's Market Influence Is Bound to the AI Trade
data.description: Former North Carolina Republican representative Patrick McHenry said Jensen Huang’s market impact and actions shape the future of AI, likening his influence to Elon Musk’s, according to Bloomberg. The Trump administration has already absolved Huang of wrongdoing.

data.title: Crypto User Reports $600,000 Loss From Trezor Wallet on iPhone 17
data.description:
A crypto holder reportedly lost $613,000 from a Trezor Safe 7 and Exodus app used with an iPhone 17 Pro Max. Blockchain data showed the transfers were signed using the owner’s authority, according to BeInCrypto, but the owner said he had not approved them and never stored his seed digitally. Tether on the TRON network accounted for about 95% of the reported loss, and a disputed 49,999 USDT transfer used the account’s owner authority rather than an old spending permission.

Apple shipped iOS 27.2.1 on Nov. 9 with a Bluetooth fix addressing a flaw that could let an attacker in Bluetooth range corrupt process memory. Onchain Lens said it found no link between the bug and the theft. Neither Trezor nor Exodus has commented. Trezor tightened its supply chain last month after a hardware wallet tampering scare involving Ledger.
